source_note: platform.openai.com/docs/pricing returns 301 to this URL. Rates were read twice from the same fetched document: once from the server-rendered HTML table cells, once from the embedded component props, which carry an explicit tier field (tier=standard read directly, not inferred from table order). Both readings agreed for every encoded model. Models whose two readings could not be bound unambiguously are listed under unencodable, never under models.
caveats: Standard service tier only. The page also publishes batch, flex, fast and ultrafast tiers; invoice lines billed at those tiers cannot be rated from this sheet.
The page prints no effective dates per rate. Validity is pinned to the retrieval date only; an invoice for an earlier period needs a sheet retrieved or archived for that period.

The page states: regional processing (data residency) endpoints are charged a 10 percent uplift for models released on or after March 5, 2026. This sheet encodes the base rates; regionally processed usage cannot be rated from it.
A null cached_input_per_1m means the page printed no cached rate for that model. Nonzero cached usage billed against such a model is INDETERMINATE, not rated at zero.
A null output_per_1m (embedding models) means the page printed no output rate. Nonzero billed output tokens on such a line is INDETERMINATE.

Validity window bounded from Wayback Machine snapshots of the source page https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing (rates read from the embedded component-prop tuples [model, input, cached, output]). valid_from 2026-10-10 is the earliest dated snapshot (web.archive.org/web/20261010103655/) on which ALL 37 encoded rates appear together with their encoded values; it is driven by gpt-rosalind-discovery, which is literally absent from the page on 2026-10-08 (web/20261008053656) and earlier and first appears on 2026-10-10. Not set earlier because discovery's rate (5/0.5/25) has no dated evidence before 2026-10-10. The other encoded rates have evidence much earlier: gpt-rosalind-research prints 'begins on October 5, 2026' and the core models (gpt-5.x, gpt-4.1, gpt-4o, o-series, embeddings) match continuously on snapshots from 2026-04-01 through 2026-10-12, so a run that does not bill gpt-rosalind-discovery could justify an earlier valid_from or a split sheet.

valid_to 2026-10-13 is the retrieval date and means LAST CONFIRMED, not confirmed unchanged after. The latest available snapshot is 2026-10-12 (web/20261012070513), which still matches all encoded rates; no snapshot exists at or after the 2026-10-13 retrieval, so no change after that date is asserted. An invoice period extending past 2026-10-13 needs a sheet re-retrieved or archived for that period.
